front: A \(1500\ \text{kg}\) car travels in a straight line at \(20\ \text{m/s}\). Determine its kinetic energy.

A hoist motor raises a \(200\ \text{kg}\) load at constant speed to a height of \(15\ \text{m}\) in \(10\ \text{s}\). Neglecting losses, find the average mechanical power delivered. Use \(g = 9.81\ \text{m/s}^{2}\).
explanation: Work done against gravity: \(W = mgh = (200)(9.81)(15) = 29{,}430\ \text{J}\). Power is work per unit time: \(P = W/t = 29{,}430/10 = 2943\ \text{W} \approx 2.94\ \text{kW}\).

front: A constant force of \(50\ \text{N}\) is applied at \(30^{\circ}\) above the horizontal to drag a crate \(8\ \text{m}\) horizontally. How much work does this force do on the crate?
explanation: Only the force component along the displacement does work: \(W = F d \cos\theta\). Substitute \(F = 50\ \text{N}\), \(d = 8\ \text{m}\), \(\theta = 30^{\circ}\): \(W = (50)(8)\cos 30^{\circ} = 400 \times 0.866 \approx 346\ \text{J}\).

front: A vehicle moves at a steady \(25\ \text{m/s}\) while its drivetrain provides a constant tractive force of \(800\ \text{N}\). Determine the power output.
explanation: For a force acting along the direction of motion, power is \(P = F v\). Substitute \(F = 800\ \text{N}\) and \(v = 25\ \text{m/s}\): \(P = (800)(25) = 20{,}000\ \text{W} = 20\ \text{kW}\).

front: A \(1500\ \text{W}\) electric motor runs continuously for \(4\ \text{hours}\). How much electrical energy does it consume, expressed in \(\text{kWh}\) and in \(\text{MJ}\)?
explanation: Energy is power times time: \(E = P t = (1.5\ \text{kW})(4\ \text{h}) = 6\ \text{kWh}\). Convert with \(1\ \text{kWh} = 3.6\ \text{MJ}\): \(E = 6 \times 3.6 = 21.6\ \text{MJ}\).

front: An electric heater connected to a \(240\ \text{V}\) supply draws \(8\ \text{A}\). Determine the power it dissipates and the total charge that flows through it in \(5\ \text{minutes}\).
explanation: Power delivered to the load: \(P = VI = (240)(8) = 1920\ \text{W}\). Charge is current times time, with \(t = 5\ \text{min} = 300\ \text{s}\): \(Q = I t = (8)(300) = 2400\ \text{C}\).

front: The charge passing a point in a wire is \(q(t) = 3t^{2} + 2t\) coulombs, with \(t\) in seconds. Find the current at \(t = 2\ \text{s}\).
explanation: Current is the time derivative of charge: \(i(t) = \dfrac{dq}{dt} = 6t + 2\). Evaluate at \(t = 2\ \text{s}\): \(i(2) = 6(2) + 2 = 14\ \text{A}\).

front: Two forces act at a single point: \(30\ \text{N}\) directed east and \(40\ \text{N}\) directed north. Find the magnitude and direction (measured from east) of the resultant.
explanation: Perpendicular components combine by the Pythagorean theorem: \(R = \sqrt{30^{2} + 40^{2}} = \sqrt{900 + 1600} = \sqrt{2500} = 50\ \text{N}\). Direction: \(\theta = \tan^{-1}(40/30) = \tan^{-1}(1.333) \approx 53.1^{\circ}\).

front: A wrench \(0.40\ \text{m}\) long has a \(150\ \text{N}\) force applied at its far end, directed perpendicular to the handle. Determine the moment (torque) about the bolt.
explanation: The moment of a force about a point is \(M = F d\) when the force is perpendicular to the moment arm. Substitute \(F = 150\ \text{N}\) and \(d = 0.40\ \text{m}\): \(M = (150)(0.40) = 60\ \text{N}\cdot\text{m}\).

front: A constant net force of \(50\ \text{N}\) acts on a \(10\ \text{kg}\) block initially at rest on a frictionless surface. Find its acceleration, its speed after \(4\ \text{s}\), and the distance travelled in that time.
explanation: Newton's second law: \(a = F/m = 50/10 = 5\ \text{m/s}^{2}\). Starting from rest, \(v = at = (5)(4) = 20\ \text{m/s}\). Distance: \(d = \tfrac{1}{2}at^{2} = \tfrac{1}{2}(5)(4)^{2} = \tfrac{1}{2}(5)(16) = 40\ \text{m}\).

front: An object is released from rest and falls \(20\ \text{m}\) with negligible air resistance. Find its speed just before impact and the time of fall. Use \(g = 9.81\ \text{m/s}^{2}\).

A \(0.15\ \text{kg}\) baseball is struck so that its speed changes from \(0\) to \(40\ \text{m/s}\) during a \(0.010\ \text{s}\) contact. Find the impulse delivered to the ball and the average force during contact.
explanation: Impulse equals the change in momentum: \(J = m\,\Delta v = (0.15)(40 - 0) = 6\ \text{kg}\cdot\text{m/s} = 6\ \text{N}\cdot\text{s}\). Average force: \(F_{avg} = J/\Delta t = 6/0.010 = 600\ \text{N}\).

front: How much heat is required to raise the temperature of \(2\ \text{kg}\) of water from \(20\,^{\circ}\text{C}\) to \(80\,^{\circ}\text{C}\)? Take the specific heat of water as \(4186\ \text{J/(kg}\cdot\text{K)}\).
explanation: Sensible heat: \(Q = m c \Delta T\), with \(\Delta T = 80 - 20 = 60\ \text{K}\). Substitute: \(Q = (2)(4186)(60) = 502{,}320\ \text{J} \approx 502\ \text{kJ}\).

front: A heat engine absorbs \(800\ \text{J}\) from a hot reservoir and rejects \(500\ \text{J}\) to a cold reservoir each cycle. Determine its thermal efficiency.
explanation: Net work per cycle: \(W = Q_H - Q_C = 800 - 500 = 300\ \text{J}\). Thermal efficiency: \(\eta = W/Q_H = 300/800 = 0.375 = 37.5\%\).

front: A power cycle operates between thermal reservoirs at \(600\ \text{K}\) and \(300\ \text{K}\). What is the maximum possible (Carnot) thermal efficiency?
explanation: Carnot efficiency depends only on the absolute reservoir temperatures: \(\eta_{\text{Carnot}} = 1 - \dfrac{T_C}{T_H}\). Substitute \(T_C = 300\ \text{K}\), \(T_H = 600\ \text{K}\): \(\eta = 1 - 300/600 = 1 - 0.5 = 0.5 = 50\%\).

front: In a well-insulated container, \(1\ \text{kg}\) of water at \(80\,^{\circ}\text{C}\) is mixed with \(3\ \text{kg}\) of water at \(20\,^{\circ}\text{C}\). Assuming no heat loss, find the final equilibrium temperature.
explanation: Energy balance (heat lost by hot water equals heat gained by cold water); the specific heats cancel: \(m_1(T_1 - T_f) = m_2(T_f - T_2)\). So \(1(80 - T_f) = 3(T_f - 20)\), giving \(80 - T_f = 3T_f - 60\). Then \(140 = 4T_f\), so \(T_f = 35\,^{\circ}\text{C}\).

front: At steady state, a mixer receives \(2\ \text{kg/s}\) of brine containing \(10\%\) salt by mass and \(3\ \text{kg/s}\) of pure water. Find the salt mass fraction of the combined outlet stream.
explanation: Overall mass balance: outlet flow \(= 2 + 3 = 5\ \text{kg/s}\). Salt (species) balance: salt in \(= 0.10(2) + 0(3) = 0.2\ \text{kg/s}\). Outlet mass fraction \(= 0.2/5 = 0.04 = 4\%\).

front: Two point charges \(Q_1 = 2\ \mu\text{C}\) and \(Q_2 = 3\ \mu\text{C}\) are \(0.10\ \text{m}\) apart in air. Find the magnitude of the electrostatic force between them. Use \(k = 8.99\times10^{9}\ \text{N}\cdot\text{m}^{2}/\text{C}^{2}\).
explanation: Coulomb's law gives \(F = \dfrac{k Q_1 Q_2}{r^{2}}\). Substituting, \(F = \dfrac{(8.99\times10^{9})(2\times10^{-6})(3\times10^{-6})}{(0.10)^{2}} = \dfrac{8.99\times10^{9}\times 6\times10^{-12}}{0.01} \approx 5.39\ \text{N}\).

front: An electron is moved through a potential difference of \(50\ \text{V}\). How much work is done on it? Use \(e = 1.602\times10^{-19}\ \text{C}\).
explanation: The work to move a charge through a potential difference is \(W = qV\). Substituting the electron charge magnitude, \(W = (1.602\times10^{-19})(50) = 8.01\times10^{-18}\ \text{J}\), equivalently \(50\ \text{eV}\).

front: Two large parallel plates are separated by \(2\ \text{mm}\) with \(100\ \text{V}\) applied across them. Assuming a uniform field, find the electric field strength between the plates.
explanation: For a uniform field between parallel plates, \(E = \dfrac{V}{d}\). Substituting \(V = 100\ \text{V}\) and \(d = 2\times10^{-3}\ \text{m}\): \(E = \dfrac{100}{0.002} = 50{,}000\ \text{V/m} = 5\times10^{4}\ \text{V/m}\).

front: A \(5\ \mu\text{C}\) point charge is placed in a uniform electric field of \(2000\ \text{V/m}\). Find the magnitude of the force on the charge.
explanation: The force on a charge in an electric field is \(F = qE\). Substituting, \(F = (5\times10^{-6})(2000) = 0.01\ \text{N}\).

front: A parallel-plate capacitor has plate area \(0.02\ \text{m}^{2}\) and plate separation \(1\ \text{mm}\) with a vacuum dielectric. Find its capacitance. Use \(\varepsilon_0 = 8.85\times10^{-12}\ \text{F/m}\).
explanation: The parallel-plate capacitance is \(C = \dfrac{\varepsilon_0 A}{d}\). Substituting, \(C = \dfrac{(8.85\times10^{-12})(0.02)}{0.001} = 1.77\times10^{-10}\ \text{F} \approx 177\ \text{pF}\).

front: A \(10\ \mu\text{F}\) capacitor is charged to \(12\ \text{V}\). How much charge is stored on it?
explanation: The charge on a capacitor is \(Q = CV\). Substituting, \(Q = (10\times10^{-6})(12) = 1.2\times10^{-4}\ \text{C} = 120\ \mu\text{C}\).

front: Find the energy stored in a \(100\ \mu\text{F}\) capacitor charged to \(50\ \text{V}\).
explanation: The energy stored in a capacitor is \(E = \tfrac{1}{2}CV^{2}\). Substituting, \(E = \tfrac{1}{2}(100\times10^{-6})(50)^{2} = \tfrac{1}{2}(100\times10^{-6})(2500) = 0.125\ \text{J}\).

front: Find the energy stored in a \(200\ \text{mH}\) inductor carrying a steady current of \(3\ \text{A}\).
explanation: The energy stored in an inductor is \(E = \tfrac{1}{2}LI^{2}\). Substituting, \(E = \tfrac{1}{2}(0.200)(3)^{2} = \tfrac{1}{2}(0.200)(9) = 0.9\ \text{J}\).

front: The current through a \(50\ \text{mH}\) inductor increases uniformly from \(0\) to \(2\ \text{A}\) in \(10\ \text{ms}\). Find the voltage across the inductor during this interval.
explanation: The inductor voltage is \(v = L\dfrac{di}{dt}\). For a uniform ramp, \(\dfrac{di}{dt} = \dfrac{2 - 0}{10\times10^{-3}} = 200\ \text{A/s}\). Thus \(v = (0.050)(200) = 10\ \text{V}\).

front: A straight wire \(0.5\ \text{m}\) long carries a current of \(4\ \text{A}\) perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field of \(0.3\ \text{T}\). Find the magnitude of the force on the wire.
explanation: The force on a current-carrying conductor is \(F = BIL\sin\theta\). With \(\theta = 90^{\circ}\), \(\sin\theta = 1\), so \(F = (0.3)(4)(0.5) = 0.6\ \text{N}\).

front: A proton (\(q = 1.602\times10^{-19}\ \text{C}\)) moves at \(1\times10^{6}\ \text{m/s}\) perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field of \(0.5\ \text{T}\). Find the magnitude of the magnetic force on it.
explanation: The magnetic force on a moving charge is \(F = qvB\sin\theta\). With \(\theta = 90^{\circ}\), \(F = (1.602\times10^{-19})(1\times10^{6})(0.5) = 8.01\times10^{-14}\ \text{N}\).

front: A spring of stiffness \(k = 400\ \text{N/m}\) is stretched \(0.05\ \text{m}\) from its natural length. Find the elastic potential energy stored.
explanation: The elastic (strain) energy stored in a linear spring is \(U = \tfrac{1}{2}kx^{2}\). Substituting, \(U = \tfrac{1}{2}(400)(0.05)^{2} = \tfrac{1}{2}(400)(0.0025) = 0.5\ \text{J}\).

front: A \(4\ \Omega\) resistor carries a steady current of \(3\ \text{A}\) for \(2\ \text{minutes}\). How much heat energy is dissipated?
explanation: The power dissipated is \(P = I^{2}R = (3)^{2}(4) = 36\ \text{W}\). Energy is power times time, with \(t = 2\ \text{min} = 120\ \text{s}\): \(E = Pt = 36 \times 120 = 4320\ \text{J}\).

front: A steel rod \(2\ \text{m}\) long is heated so that its temperature rises by \(50\ ^{\circ}\text{C}\). If the coefficient of linear thermal expansion is \(\alpha = 1.2\times10^{-5}\ /^{\circ}\text{C}\), find the increase in length.
explanation: The thermal expansion of a rod is \(\Delta L = \alpha L\,\Delta T\). Substituting, \(\Delta L = (1.2\times10^{-5})(2)(50) = 1.2\times10^{-3}\ \text{m} = 1.2\ \text{mm}\).

front: How much heat is required to completely melt \(0.5\ \text{kg}\) of ice at \(0\ ^{\circ}\text{C}\)? The latent heat of fusion of water is \(L_f = 3.34\times10^{5}\ \text{J/kg}\).
explanation: For a phase change at constant temperature, \(Q = mL_f\). Substituting, \(Q = (0.5)(3.34\times10^{5}) = 1.67\times10^{5}\ \text{J} = 167\ \text{kJ}\).
